config_valid.expected_solution: Valid drift report covers Terraform v1.7.0 core and terraform-provider-aws v5.31.0 and is grounded in files that exist at those revs. Each entry must include config_key (the resource attribute causing the phantom diff), terraform_core_behavior with terraform_core_file from the terraform repo (internal/terraform/node_resource_plan_instance.go, internal/terraform/context_plan.go, or internal/plans/objchange/objchange.go — the eval_diff.go/eval_refresh.go files of older cores no longer exist at v1.7.0), provider_behavior with provider_file from the aws provider (internal/service/iam/policy.go or internal/service/ec2/vpc_security_group.go — the pre-v4 internal/services layout is gone), and an impact statement describing the phantom diff. The report must be valid JSON.
evaluation_criteria: Must produce valid JSON parsable by json.loads with a top-level drift_points array
Must cite at least one core-side file that exists at v1.7.0: internal/terraform/node_resource_plan_instance.go, internal/terraform/context_plan.go, or internal/plans/objchange/objchange.go
Must cite at least one provider-side file that exists at v5.31.0: internal/service/iam/policy.go or internal/service/ec2/vpc_security_group.go
Each drift_point must contain config_key, terraform_core_behavior, terraform_core_file, provider_behavior, provider_file, impact

drift_points.expected_solution: Drift points between Terraform core v1.7.0 and terraform-provider-aws v5.31.0. (1) JSON policy normalization: aws_iam_policy in internal/service/iam/policy.go stores the policy document as a string; AWS returns the canonicalized form on Read, so the schema counters with DiffSuppressFunc verify.SuppressEquivalentPolicyDiffs, DiffSuppressOnRefresh: true, and a StateFunc running structure.NormalizeJsonString (policy.go:85-91), plus verify.PolicyToSet on Read (policy.go:208). Terraform core plans in internal/terraform/node_resource_plan_instance.go using the objchange machinery; a phantom diff appears whenever the provider suppression layer and AWS canonicalization rules drift. (2) Set-vs-list rule ordering: aws_security_group ingress/egress in internal/service/ec2/vpc_security_group.go are schema.TypeSet blocks hashed by SecurityGroupRuleHash (vpc_security_group.go:128); the provider Read returns AWS-ordered rules and re-aligns them via MatchRules. When the hash inputs change (e.g. optional rule fields) or the returned rule shape aggregates differently, the set hash differs and core's set comparison plans a phantom update.
evaluation_criteria: Must reference internal/service/iam/policy.go as the aws_iam_policy Read/schema location and name verify.SuppressEquivalentPolicyDiffs as its normalization hook
Must reference internal/service/ec2/vpc_security_group.go as the aws_security_group Read location and name SecurityGroupRuleHash as the rule-set hash
Must call out at least two specific drift mechanisms (JSON canonicalization vs byte comparison, set hashing vs returned rule ordering)

expected_values.expected_solution: Expected behavior: (1) JSON policy attributes should round-trip: the provider in internal/service/iam/policy.go applies DiffSuppressFunc=verify.SuppressEquivalentPolicyDiffs with DiffSuppressOnRefresh and StateFunc=structure.NormalizeJsonString so the stored state and the AWS-returned canonical JSON compare equal, and Read rebuilds the value with verify.PolicyToSet; Terraform core in internal/terraform/node_resource_plan_instance.go builds the planned value via objchange.ProposedNew (internal/plans/objchange/objchange.go:31) and validates the applied result with AssertObjectCompatible (internal/plans/objchange/compatible.go:29), so a suppressed difference must never surface as a proposed change. (2) Security-group rules should hash deterministically: SecurityGroupRuleHash in internal/service/ec2/vpc_security_group.go must cover every material rule field so the set comparison produces zero-change output when nothing material changed. (3) Server-side defaults should be schema-marked Computed so core does not propose changes for attributes the user never set. The override chain is: provider schema/Read in internal/service/<type>/*.go -> state stored on disk -> core plan in internal/terraform/node_resource_plan_instance.go via internal/plans/objchange -> rendered plan output.
evaluation_criteria: Must cite a real core-side plan/diff file at v1.7.0 (node_resource_plan_instance.go, context_plan.go, or objchange.go)
Must name the core comparison machinery: objchange (ProposedNew / AssertObjectCompatible)
Must name the provider normalization machinery: structure.NormalizeJsonString, verify.PolicyToSet, or DiffSuppressOnRefresh
Must explain the override chain: provider Read -> state -> core plan/diff -> plan output
